correctness.rationale: For a two-colouring of \(K_n\), every edge has \(2n-4\) adjacent edges, so both colour counts must equal \(n-2\). If \(d(v)\) is the red degree, this gives \(d(u)+d(v)=n\) on red edges and \(n-2\) on blue edges. For odd \(n\), three pairwise degree sums cannot all be odd. For even \(n\), all degrees have the same parity, differ by at most two, and exactly two values occur; one degree class must be a singleton. The red graph is therefore a star or a clique plus an isolated vertex, and the degree gap forces \(n=4\). The submitted three-colour constructions for \(n=3,5,7\), and the equitable three-part construction for \(n=6\) and \(n\ge8\), meet the threshold. An independent exhaustive replay of every two-colouring for \(K_3,K_4,K_5\) confirmed that only \(K_4\) admits two colours.
